Allocation, lifetime, teardown and error recovery for type objects, collections, pages and folios.

findings.text: Type information stores variable element count in its low 24 bits, and function linkage is read through that same low portion.
Kind flag is the top bit of the type information word, obtained by shifting by 31.
Member offset packs bit offset in the low 24 bits and bitfield width in the bits above that range.
Identifier collections live in object section .BTF_ids, and the extended set flag for kernel functions has value one.
Trap classification uses 0 for none, 1 for warning and 2 for fatal.
Linux build salt note number is 0x100 and maximum build identifier size is 20.

Socket type identifiers run consecutively from zero as BTF_SOCK_TYPE_INET, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_INET_CONN, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_INET_REQ, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_INET_TW, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_REQ, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_SOCK, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_SOCK_COMMON, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_TCP, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_TCP_REQ, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_TCP_TW, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_TCP6, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_UDP, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_UDP6, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_UNIX, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_MPTCP, BTF_SOCK_TYPE_SOCKET, closed by MAX_BTF_SOCK_TYPE, each originally paired with a structure name in the same order.

Tracing type identifiers run consecutively from zero as BTF_TRACING_TYPE_TASK, BTF_TRACING_TYPE_FILE, BTF_TRACING_TYPE_VMA, closed by MAX_BTF_TRACING_TYPE, each originally paired with a structure name in the same order.

Field descriptor holds a count plus two type level offsets, a member size, and a count plus one per member offset, while the iterator pairs that descriptor with a cursor pointer, member index, offset index and remaining length.
Plain identifier set is a count followed by packed identifiers, and extended set is a count plus flags followed by identifier flag pairs.

Block vector entry references a page with length and offset, the iterator carries sector, residual size, vector index and intra entry offset with packed four byte alignment, and the exhaustive iterator adds current entry, index and completion count.
Reader state combines buffer, size and error with either file backed cursor of file, folio, address, folio offset and fault permission, or memory backed data pointer and length.
Member bit position uses packed decoding only when the containing type carries the kind flag, otherwise the stored value is the direct offset, and bitfield width is zero without that flag.
Variable type payload for members, arrays, enumerations, parameters, tags and section info starts immediately after the fixed header, with indexed member access offset from that base.
Membership in plain and extended identifier sets is decided by binary search over sorted storage, with extended search yielding the matching pair location.

Without runtime type support, lookups and naming yield null or false, relocation and iteration report not supported, destructor search reports missing, context and sameness checks fail, base association does nothing, while registration helpers report success.
Structure pointer recognition rejects non pointers and otherwise tests the modifier stripped target for structure kind.
List and set construction emits symbols and fixed size slots into the identifier section, with start markers opening the collection and end markers sizing it and declaring external visibility.
When collection support is unavailable, lists become local arrays of 128 entries or single entry, and sets become zeroed local records with kernel function sets premarked.
Optional build time assertion either evaluates to zero or selects compile time versus runtime trapping based on whether its condition is constant.
Fallback bug lookup never matches an address, any report is classified as fatal, file location resolves to empty, and once state clearing does nothing.
Warning status is determined by testing a dedicated warning bit in the bug entry flags.
Corruption probe returns its input after dumping a supplied object on positive indication and then either logging with a halt or issuing a warning depending on configuration.

Compile time checks cover zero expression trapping with message, power of two validation with and without zero rejection, invalid expression sizing, message assertion, unconditional failure, static assertion and structure offset verification.
Vector initialization assigns page, length and offset directly, or splits a folio byte offset into page index and remainder, or converts a virtual address into its page and intra page displacement.
Single page view of a multi page position exposes the containing page, intra page offset and length limited to the page remainder, assembled into a fresh vector entry.
Iteration starts from a given position, presents the current slice while bytes remain, and consumes the presented length each step, with exhaustive initialization resetting progress.
Mapping, copying and clearing through a vector delegate to page operations addressed by the stored page, offset and length, with direct virtual access requiring low memory.
Each header uses a unique include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.
Object dumping and virtual image identifier initialization are no operation placeholders in these configurations.
Build salt note emission has two alternate encodings differing in note macro selection and string handling.
Field traversal distinguishes identifier iteration from string iteration.
Inline helpers expose type length, linkage, flags, member positions, payload slices and identifier set tests.
Query and registration helpers expose structure operations lookup, type by identifier, relocation, field iteration, name resolution, kernel function sets, destructor search and context checks.
Bug helpers expose warning testing, address lookup, trap reporting, location decoding, object dumping and corruption checking.
Block vector helpers expose initialization from page, folio or virtual address, single page slicing, iteration, local mapping, copying, clearing and direct access.
Build helpers expose salt notes, compile time assertions, identifier limits and file reading state.
Identifier macros expose list, set and kernel function collection definition with single, unused and global variants.
Direct virtual access from a vector is unsafe for high memory pages and oversized folio lengths risk truncation, both reported via warnings.
Positive corruption indication either halts after logging or warns, so callers must treat a true result as a possibly fatal event.
Collection lifecycle opens with a start marker, accumulates fixed size identifier slots, then closes with an end marker that finalizes size and visibility.
Traversal begins from an initial position with residual bytes, repeatedly exposes the current slice, consumes its length, and terminates when no bytes remain.
External mapping dependency for vector local access.
Alternate external mapping dependency for vector local access.
External page copy out dependency for vector reads.
External page copy in dependency for vector writes.
External page clearing dependency for vector zeroing.
External minimum selection dependency for slice length capping.
External intra page displacement dependency for virtual address conversion.
External page address dependency for direct vector access.
Alternate external page address dependency for direct vector access.
